tasks.title: Define the canonical host-surface model, capability negotiation, and bounded fallback
criteria: AC11: Supported, unsupported, partial, unknown, stale, contradictory, and changed-mid-run capability profiles record host/version, source/confidence, selected surface, limitations, and fallback and select deterministic behavior without false support.

AC12: Disabling PiP, visualization, carousel, approval, sandbox, hosting, browser, and side-panel capabilities independently preserves canonical values, evidence, audit, gates, and reachable safe actions in an accessible bounded fallback that names unavailable rather than user-declined.

tasks.title: Publish truthful PiP, agent topology, and authoritative native approval receipts
criteria: AC1: On every host profile supporting persistent PiP, one active workflow opens one session showing workflow identity, stage, active/completed work, attention, and last update; ordered changes are reflected and the session closes automatically on completion, cancellation, or failure, while completed static work never opens PiP.

AC2: Complete, incremental, delayed, absent, malformed, and cross-provider usage fixtures show observed raw/effective tokens with scope/source or explicit partial/unavailable status, reconcile to the canonical token record, and never fabricate zero or estimates.

AC3: Serial, parallel, mixed-wave, retry, cancellation, failure, and resume fixtures visualize every dispatched agent with stable task/slot identity, role, scope, relationship, state, attention, and outcome matching the canonical audit record without duplicates or phantoms.

AC4: Plan, design, dynamic-validation, review, and signoff approval fixtures show the exact decision, reason, target/revision, relevant evidence, consequences, owner, and approvability, with at most two primary inline actions and richer content moved to detail/fullscreen.

AC5: A native approval advances state exactly once only when an authenticated human receipt is bound to the current decision, actor, target, and revision; stale, duplicate, replayed, disabled, unauthenticated, wrong-revision, or presentation-only actions cannot advance.

tasks.title: Project native dashboard components with deterministic carousels and accessible conversational layouts
criteria: AC6: Canonical workflow, DoR, dependency/impact, agents, lenses, criteria, findings, validation, artifacts, and gate snapshots project on Codex and Claude with equal values, ordering semantics, provenance, and actions despite allowed host-specific styling.

AC7: Dataset fixtures containing 0, 1, 3, 8, 9, 120, and multi-page items use deterministic 3-to-8-item visually consistent carousel pages where needed, expose concise metadata plus total/current position, support navigation/filtering, and preserve every stable item identity.

AC8: Inline structure and viewport tests prove cards are single-purpose, responsive, have no nested scrolling/deep navigation, preserve the conversational composer, respect the two-primary-action limit, and use detail/fullscreen for rich multi-step exploration.

AC13: Automated accessibility, keyboard, text-scaling, reduced-motion, light/dark theme, and responsive viewport checks prove native/fallback surfaces use system tokens/fonts/layout, WCAG AA contrast, semantic labels, alt text, visible focus, and non-color status cues.

tasks.title: Run design, build, and review previews in pinned private disposable scopes
criteria: AC9: One authorized design, build, and dynamic-review scenario opens an interactive pinned working preview in the host-integrated browser or side panel where supported, records preview identity/lifecycle, and links observed behavior to canonical evidence.

AC10: Valid, unavailable, denied, build-failed, timeout, attempted-push, escaped-path, external-network, and teardown preview fixtures prove execution occurs only in a registered pinned bounded disposable scope, never pushes or changes the source checkout/remotes, and fails safely with auditable outcomes.

tasks.title: Ship capability declarations, native guidance, and cross-host fallback compatibility
criteria: AC14: Concurrent update, reconnect/resume, stale UI, duplicate event, host switch, and terminal-close fixtures prove PiP, fan-out, approvals, dashboards, carousels, previews, fallbacks, and artifacts reference one workflow/run, target, revision, task/slot identity, evidence, gate state, and ordered audit history.

AC15: Existing non-native design, build, review, status, approval, and artifact golden scenarios plus the native-capability matrix pass without lost evidence, weaker gates, removed tests, skips, xfails, loosened assertions, or reclassified failures.
